strings.p9.title: Reading the data
strings.p9.intro: Where the data comes from, how it is counted, and what to watch for. Figures on this page are as of the August 2026 data.
strings.p9.source.title: Data origin
strings.p9.source.p1: All data comes from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's Federal Workforce Data. OPM publishes three monthly files: a snapshot of every employee at the end of the month, the hires (accessions) and the departures (separations).
strings.p9.source.p2: The dashboard covers October 2011 through the latest month OPM has published, and is updated when OPM releases new files.
strings.p9.source.p3: Departments, agencies and subelements are grouped by OPM's codes, not by name, and each is shown under its latest name with its whole history. Within Defense, OPM reports four agencies: the Departments of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force, and a fourth it also names Department of Defense, shown here as Department of Defense (DD).
strings.p9.source.p4: Each record is one person, but OPM's files have no personal identifier, so the dashboard cannot follow anyone from month to month or from one agency to another.
strings.p9.count.title: How things are counted
strings.p9.count.p1: Employees are counted at the end of each month. For a quarter or a year, the count is the one at the end of its last month, never an average or a sum.
strings.p9.count.p2: Hires and departures are counted in the month they took effect, not the month OPM processed them. 97.9% of hires and 94.4% of departures are processed in the month they take effect.
strings.p9.count.p3: The latest three months are provisional: late actions can still add to them, so they are always marked.
strings.p9.count.p4: Years run from October to September, the federal fiscal year. A year or quarter still in progress is marked partial and covers only the months published so far.
strings.p9.count.p5: Change in employees and hires minus departures come from different files, so they do not always match. The dashboard shows both and never adjusts one to fit the other.
strings.p9.count.p6: Government totals include every transfer between agencies: a transfer is a departure for one agency and a hire for another. Transfers out have exceeded transfers in every year except fiscal year 2022, when Defense's move of military treatment facilities recorded 38,613 transfers in.
strings.p9.rates.title: Rates and categories
strings.p9.rates.p1: A departure rate is the number of people who left, divided by the average number of employees over the same months, using month-end counts. A hire rate works the same way.
strings.p9.rates.p2: You can choose how a rate is measured: past 12 months, fiscal year, or annual pace.
strings.p9.rates.p3: When a rate is based on fewer than 30 employees on average it is shown with a flag, because a few people can move it a lot.
strings.p9.rates.p4: Each departure has one reason, from OPM's separation codes: transfer to another agency, quit, retirement, reduction in force, termination or expired appointment, or other.
strings.p9.rates.p5: Departures under the Deferred Resignation Program are flagged by OPM. In the "why people left" charts they are their own reason and are not counted again under the others; elsewhere they count under their original reason.
strings.p9.issues.title: Known data issues
strings.p9.issues.intro: Problems found in OPM's files and how the dashboard handles them.
strings.p9.issues.kdi001: Length of service counted from 1900: in OPM's files from June 2024 to July 2025, 7,665 departures and 5,391 hires show 124 to 126 years of service. They are treated as unknown; the Look-Up shows them as published.
strings.p9.issues.kdi002: Occupational category missing: from June 2024, OPM's departure files leave the broad occupational category empty on most records, so it is not used.
strings.p9.issues.kdi003: Duplicate rows: a few Defense units in May and June 2026 have exact duplicate rows, which overstate Defense in June 2026 by about 13,000. They are counted as published and flagged.
strings.p9.issues.kdi004: Housing and Urban Development rows from October 2024 to March 2025 have no department code; they are placed in HUD by their agency code and flagged.
strings.p9.issues.kdi005: Air Force rows from February to April 2015 have no department code; they are placed in Defense by their agency code and flagged.
strings.p9.issues.kdi006: OPM reports that Defense data were incomplete in June and July 2026; those months are flagged for Defense and the government total.
strings.p9.issues.kdi007: Grade is withheld on about 0.1% of employee records; grade groups show it as unknown.
strings.p9.issues.kdi008: One hire in the August 2016 file has no department code; it is placed by its agency code and flagged.
strings.p9.issues.kdi009: A few records show more than 100 years of service outside the 1900 problem; they are treated as unknown.
strings.p9.issues.kdi010: Seven hires in 2026 files show a negative length of service; they are treated as unknown.
strings.p9.issues.kdi011: Job series missing: some records have a blank or invalid job series (most years under 0.15%; among departures, 1.7% in fiscal 2016, 0.6% in 2024, 2.8% in 2025 and 1.9% in 2026). They are shown as "Not reported" in every occupation list, never dropped.
strings.p9.breaks.title: Known breaks
strings.p9.breaks.p1: For each department and fiscal year, the dashboard compares the change in employees with hires minus departures. Where they differ by more than 5% of the average number of employees and more than 20 people, the year is listed below. Most come from September departures that leave the employee count in October: in September 2025, 132,949 departures took effect, 106,883 of them deferred resignations, while the employee count fell 28,342 in September and 92,685 in October.
strings.p9.redact.title: Withheld values
strings.p9.redact.p1: OPM withholds pay, duty location and some other fields for many employees: about 47% of employee records in August 2026, including every Defense record. The dashboard therefore shows no pay or location breakdowns; the Look-Up shows REDACTED where a value was withheld.
strings.p9.revisions.title: Revised files
strings.p9.revisions.p1: OPM sometimes reissues a month's files; in October 2026 it reissued every file. When that happens the dashboard reloads them, and figures can change.

strings.p10.intro: Which jobs agencies are hiring for and losing, by job series or occupational family, as OPM classifies them.
strings.p10.level.label: Group by
strings.p10.hired.title: Most hired
strings.p10.departed.title: Most departed
strings.p10.sort.label: Sort by
strings.p10.note.notReported: "Not reported" counts records where OPM left the job series or family blank or invalid. See Reading the data.
strings.p10.note.moves: Employees also move between job series without being hired or leaving, so the change in employees in an occupation can differ from its hires minus departures.
strings.p10.note.seriesBelowGov: Single job series over time is shown government-wide only. Below that level, open the Look-Up for the records.
